extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, patent practitioners, and USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for preparing, submitting, and recording assignment and related documents at the United States Patent and Trademark Office, and for establishing an assignee's right to take action in patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment must be in writing (35 U.S.C. 261)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for patent, patents, or any interest therein, shall be assignable in law by an instrument in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certificate of acknowledgment (properly executed/apostilled) is prima facie evidence of execution. An assignment that is not recorded in the PTO within three months of its date (or prior to a subsequent purchaser/mortgagee) is void against that subsequent purchaser or mortgagee for valuable consideration without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of assignment and recorded document (37 CFR 3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment means a transfer by a party of all or part of its right, title and interest in a patent, patent application, registered mark or a mark for which an application to register has been filed. Document means a document which a party requests to be recorded in the Office pursuant to § 3.11 and which affects some interest in an application, patent, or registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to determine whether a paper is an assignable interest and whether it is recordable under Part 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation is ministerial and provides public notice (37 CFR 3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office records assignments and other documents relating to interests in patents and patent applications; recording provides legal notice to the public but is a ministerial act and is not an Office determination of the validity or effect of the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a patent to issue to an assignee, the assignment must have been recorded or filed for recordation in accordance with 37 CFR 3.11. Recording an assignment in the assignment records does not, by itself, permit the assignee to take action in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment document must be a copy or extract (37 CFR 3.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accept and record only a copy of an original assignment or other document; original documents must not be submitted because recorded documents are not returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submissions: submit digitized images (TIFF or other Director-prescribed form); when printed at 8.5x11 or A4, document must be legible with 1-inch margins. Paper/facsimile: one side per page, flexible strong white non-shiny durable paper, same paper sizes and margins. Ensure legibility—an illegible copy will yield an illegible recorded document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English documents require signed English translation (37 CFR 3.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accept and record non-English language documents only if accompanied by an English translation signed by the individual making the translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the assignment is not in English, include a signed translation with the submission; otherwise the Office will not record the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments must identify the patent or application (37 CFR 3.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment relating to a patent must identify the patent by patent number; assignments to national/international applications must identify the application number; if executed before filing the application, the assignment must identify the inventor(s) and title so there is no mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application or provisional filing numbers are not yet known, draft the assignment to permit later insertion of the application number/filing date (example wording provided in MPEP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign assignee may designate a domestic representative (35 U.S.C. 293; 37 CFR 3.61)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee not domiciled in the United States may designate a person residing in the U.S. on whom process or notice may be served; the designation should be a separate paper labeled 'Designation of Domestic Representative' and signed per 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the designation separately from the assignment document so it is entered into the application or patent file record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee address required on cover sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The address of the assignee may be recited in the assignment document and must be given in the required cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a complete mailing/correspondence address for the party receiving the interest on the cover sheet to ensure proper processing and contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording fee rules (37 CFR 3.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee is required for each application, patent and registration against which the document is recorded as identified in the cover sheet, except in specified Executive Order 9424 circumstances or where the document is identified as not affecting title and submitted by fax or electronically as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted electronically the fee may be $0 (check current fee schedule). For paper or facsimile submissions, consult current fee schedule in 37 CFR 1.21(h)(2). Check the USPTO website for up-to-date fees; see MPEP §§ 302.08–302.10 for submission methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every assignment submission must be accompanied by a single cover sheet (37 CFR 3.28; 3.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document submitted for recording must include a single cover sheet referring to those patents/applications against which the document is to be recorded; lacking a completed cover sheet the document will be returned for proper completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent cover sheet must contain: (A) name of party conveying the interest, (B) name and address of party receiving the interest, (C) description of the interest conveyed or transaction, (D) patent/application numbers or indication document is filed with an application, (E) correspondence name/address, (F) date executed, (G) signature of submitting party. Additional recommended contents: number of items and total fee, and for joint research agreements, identification of parties and execution date. Cover sheets should not refer to both patents and trademarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet signature and electronic signature rules (37 CFR 3.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature of the party submitting the document is required; for electronic submissions, the signer must either place a symbol between forward slashes (e.g., /Thomas O’Malley III/) in the signature block or sign using another form of electronic signature specified by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using electronic submission, follow the electronic signature formats acceptable to the Office to avoid rejection of the cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment may contain statements required for oath/declaration (35 U.S.C. 115(e); 37 CFR 1.63(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), 363, or 385 on or after Sept. 16, 2012, an assignment may contain the statements required in an oath or declaration and, if recorded in assignment records, the assignment may be utilized as the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If intending to use an assignment as the oath/declaration, include a conspicuous indication of that intent on the cover sheet (see 37 CFR 3.31(h)) and ensure the assignment contains the necessary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment records accessibility and public inspection (37 CFR 1.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment records for patents, published patent applications, registrations, and certain applications are open to public inspection at the USPTO; pre-May 1, 1957 patent assignment records are maintained by NARA and are obtainable from NARA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records for assignments recorded June 1998 and later are viewable on the USPTO website; earlier records require ordering and providing reel/frame identifiers. Documents covering multiple items (e.g., both trademarks and patents) become open to public inspection if any part is open (whole-document rule). Confidential pending applications not open under 1.11/1.14 require written authority or successful petition to obtain copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: When assignment records for earlier (parent) applications are open
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application on which a patent was granted is a division, continuation, or continuation-in-part of an earlier application, the assignment records of that earlier application will be open to public inspection because copies or access may be supplied to the earlier application pursuant to 37 CFR 1.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider parent-file assignments when researching title or public records, not just the immediate application or patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making an assignment of record vs. making an assignee the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment can be recorded in the assignment records to provide public notice; separately, an assignment can be entered into the file of a patent application/patent to permit the assignee to ‘take action’ under 37 CFR 1.46 and 3.81(a). Recording in assignment records alone does not permit the assignee to take action in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To permit an assignee to prosecute an application, file the appropriate request to change the applicant (37 CFR 1.46(c)(2)) and other required statements so the assignee is made the applicant of record in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing assignee's ownership to take action for post‑Sept‑16‑2012 applications (37 CFR 3.73(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an assignee who was not the original applicant first seeks to take action in an application filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, the assignee must establish ownership to the satisfaction of the Director via a 37 CFR 3.73(c) statement and must file a request to change the applicant and an application data sheet specifying the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 3.73(c) statement must contain either (A) documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee (and affirm that such evidence was or concurrently is submitted for recordation), or (B) specify by reel and frame number where such evidence is recorded in the Office. Documents submitted to establish ownership are required to be recorded or submitted for recordation as a condition to permitting the assignee to take action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of ownership establishment (37 CFR 3.73(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission establishing ownership and the request for change of applicant must be submitted prior to, or at the same time as, the paper requesting or taking action; if submitted later, that later date will be the date of the request or action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine the 3.73(c) ownership statement with the action-requesting paper when possible to avoid effectless submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign the 37 CFR 3.73(c) submission (37 CFR 3.73(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The ownership submission must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee. Acceptable signers include: (A) a person with apparent authority (officers are presumed to have authority), (B) any person if the submission states that the person is authorized to act, (C) a patent practitioner of record, or (D) a person empowered by an organizational resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authority is unclear, include evidence (e.g., corporate resolution) or an explicit statement of authority. A power of attorney to a practitioner does not alone make that practitioner an official signer unless the practitioner is of record or appointed in the accompanying power of attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple/partial assignees must each establish ownership (37 CFR 3.73(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the right, title and interest is held by more than one assignee (partial assignees) each must provide a 3.73(c) submission. Each submission must either (A) specify (by percentage) the extent of the ownership interest so the Office can account for the entire right, title and interest, or (B) identify the parties (including inventors who own interest) who together own the entire right, title and interest and state that all identified parties together own the entire interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If extents are unspecified, the Office may refuse to accept the submission as establishing ownership interest. Ensure the combination of submissions accounts for the entirety of ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling conflicting 37 CFR 3.73(c) statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more purported assignees file conflicting 3.73(c) statements in an application or other proceeding, the Director will determine which purported assignee, if any, is permitted to be the controlling assignee for prosecution. If contested on the record, the proceeding may be forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration for procedural resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties filing conflicting statements may consider filing their own applications if not permitted to control prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing applications and ownership statements
rubrics_metrics.description: When an assignee files a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b), the application papers must contain either a copy of a statement filed under pre‑AIA 3.73(b) or 3.73(c) in the parent application, or a newly executed 3.73(c) statement; a CPA under 1.53(d) may rely on the parent application statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure ownership documentation is carried forward or newly filed to avoid interruptions in prosecution rights for continuing proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples when ownership must be established
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership must be established under 37 CFR 3.73(c) in situations such as when the assignee (who is not the applicant) signs a request for status, gives a power to inspect an application, appoints its own registered attorney/agent to prosecute, signs a disclaimer, consents to filing a reissue application, or signs a Fee Transmittal (PTOL‑85B). Effective Sept. 16, 2012, juristic entities must be represented by a patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an assignee will perform substantive prosecution activities or filings listed above, prepare and file the 3.73(c) statement and related requests in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples when ownership need not be established
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner need not establish ownership under 37 CFR 3.73(c) for certain ministerial or limited functions such as signing a small entity statement, signing a statement of common ownership of two inventions, signing NASA/DOE property rights statements, signing certain affidavits where the inventor is unavailable, signing a certificate under 1.8, or filing a request for reexamination under 1.510.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check MPEP cross-references (e.g., §§ cited) to confirm whether 3.73(c) is required for a specific paper or sequence of actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PTO/AIA/96 may be used to establish ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/AIA/96 may be used to make the 37 CFR 3.73(c) submission establishing ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the Office-provided form helps ensure required fields and statements are present; do not submit duplicate copies of the 3.73(c) statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing is distinct from assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing transfers a bundle of rights less than the entire ownership interest (e.g., limited by time, geography, or field of use). An exclusive license may prevent the owner from competing with the licensee but is not an assignment of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat a license as an assignment; licenses are contractual and may be recorded but do not transfer ownership unless the instrument effectuates an assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint and individual ownership rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual ownership occurs where one party owns the entire interest. Joint ownership exists where multiple parties together own the entire right, title and interest (e.g., multiple partial assignees, multiple inventors not assigned, or combinations thereof). Each individual inventor may only assign the interest held by that individual; partial assignees likewise may assign only their share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All parties holding any portion of ownership must act together as a composite entity in patent matters before the Office unless proper changes of applicant/recordation make a single assignee the sole owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will not open only parts of a multi‑item document to public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recorded document contains two or more items, any one of which alone would be open to inspection, then the entire document will be open. Thus, a document covering both trademarks and patents will be available to the public if any part is published or patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing combined documents, be aware that inclusion of any publicly open item will make the whole document public; separate patent and trademark cover sheets and copies if needed to avoid unintended disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for copies should identify reel and frame numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: An order for a copy of an assignment or other document should identify the reel and frame number where the assignment or document is recorded; if not specified, an extra search charge will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify reel/frame when ordering copies to avoid additional fees and delays.
